title: Common AI workloads: generative, agentic, text, speech, vision and extraction
learningObjective: Identify scenarios for common AI workloads, including generative and agentic AI, text analysis, speech, computer vision and information extraction.
foundation: Generative AI creates new content (text, code, images) from a prompt. Agentic AI goes further: an agent uses a model plus tools to take steps and complete a task.
Text analysis finds meaning in text (sentiment, entities, topics). Speech turns speech into text and text into speech. Computer vision understands images and video.
Information extraction pulls structured data (fields like invoice total, date) out of documents, images, audio and video.
Microsoft Foundry provides models for generative and agentic AI, plus Foundry Tools (formerly Azure AI services): Azure Language, Speech, Vision, Translator and Content Understanding.
engineer: Generative AI scenarios: drafting emails and documents, summarising, answering questions over your data (RAG), writing code, creating images. Agentic AI scenarios: booking, ordering, research assistants, IT helpdesk automation: tasks needing tools, multiple steps and sometimes several agents.

Text analysis scenarios: review sentiment, extracting entities from contracts, detecting and redacting PII, language detection, summarising long reports. Speech scenarios: captions, call transcription and analytics, voice assistants, reading text aloud, speech translation.

Computer vision scenarios: image captions and tags for accessibility and search, object detection for retail shelves, OCR of receipts, visual inspection, answering questions about photos. Information extraction scenarios: invoices, forms, ID documents, call recordings, video indexing.

Choosing the approach: a prompt to a generative model is flexible; a Foundry Tool gives task-specific, consistent results with confidence scores; an agent adds tools and actions. Many solutions combine them, for example speech-to-text, then a model, then text-to-speech.

animation.caption: Match scenarios to AI workloads, and decide between a model, an agent or a Foundry Tool.

example.title: A retailer's AI map
body: Marketing drafts product descriptions with a chat model (generative). A returns agent checks the order system and creates labels (agentic).
Azure Language scores review sentiment; Azure Speech transcribes support calls; shelf cameras use object detection; Content Understanding reads supplier invoices.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Foundry portal > your project: explore Models, Agents, and Foundry Tools playgrounds (Language, Speech, Vision, Content Understanding).

troubleshooting.fix: Build an agent with a booking function or API tool.

troubleshooting.cause: A generative prompt without fixed scoring.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Azure Language sentiment for consistent scores.

comparisons.difference: Generative produces content; agentic plans and acts with tools.
Text analysis finds meaning in text; extraction fills defined fields from documents and media.

misconceptions.myth: Every AI feature needs a large language model.
misconceptions.reality: Prebuilt Foundry Tools often fit better.
Agents call tools and take actions.
It covers captions, objects, OCR and more.

architectureDecisions: Identify the workload before choosing services.
Prefer prebuilt tools for standard tasks needing consistency.
Add agents only when actions or tools are needed.
